name: WEDOS | Protection & Cache Performance
author: wedos.com

sections.description:
The plugin connects your website to WEDOS Global Protection and keeps an eye on its health. Setup is guided step by step and suits non-technical site owners: the plugin prefills your domain, shows exactly the DNS records WEDOS Protection asks for and nothing is registered until you confirm it.

Protection

  • Cloud WAF and DDoS protection: harmful traffic is filtered on the WEDOS network before it reaches your server.
  • Free setup or your existing service: a domain without protection gets a free WEDOS Protection service after your consent. A domain that is already protected (also in your own WEDOS account) is only displayed, never registered again.
  • Dashboard: protection status, the DNS records to set and traffic analytics.

Speed

  • WP-CDN: WordPress core, WooCommerce, plugin and theme files served from the WEDOS CDN. A file is rewritten only when its SHA-256 hash matches the CDN copy. Off until you enable it.
  • Page Local Cache: rendered pages stored as static HTML on your server.

Security checks

  • Vulnerabilities: installed plugins, themes and WordPress core compared daily with a database of publicly known vulnerabilities. The comparison runs on your server.
  • Recommendations: concrete fixes based on your own traffic, applied only after you confirm them.
  • UpdraftCentral key compromise: detection of the October 2026 backdoor, with the steps to take. Read-only: the plugin never changes other plugins or accounts.

Links

  • WEDOS Global
  • Knowledge Base
  • Community Help

The service is provided by WEDOS Group SA, 7 Rue Robert Stumper, L-2557 Luxembourg, EU: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

External services

No personal data of your visitors is ever transmitted.

WEDOS Global Protection (plugin.wedos.global)

  • Used to verify domain ownership (a verification file the plugin writes to /.well-known/), to register the protection service and to read its status and traffic statistics.
  • Data sent: domain name, server IP address, admin email address, a request ID and this installation’s private API key (it proves the request comes from this site; only its SHA-256 hash is published in the verification file).
  • A protection service is registered only after you click “Activate protection + CDN” and confirm the consent dialog.

WEDOS CDN (wp-cdn.wedos.com)

  • Only when WP-CDN is enabled: serves static files of WordPress core, WooCommerce, plugins and themes, and the manifest with their SHA-256 hashes.
  • No data about visitors is transmitted.

Anonymous telemetry (plugin.wedos.global)

  • Only when you opt in: plugin version, WordPress version and number of rewritten files, once a day. No domain, IP address or personal data.

Subscriptions (plugin.wedos.global) and billing (FastSpring)

  • Used only when you start a trial or buy a paid plan. Data sent: domain name, admin email address, plan.
  • Orders are processed by FastSpring (fastspring.com) as the merchant of record; see FastSpring’s privacy policy.
  • The free plan works without any subscription. When a trial ends, the plugin keeps working on the free plan.

Vulnerability database (utils.wedos.tools)

  • Downloaded once a day (compiled from the Wordfence Intelligence feed, CC BY-ND 4.0). Nothing about your site is sent.

Website performance check (utils.wedos.tools)

  • Once a day measures the public loading speed of your website for the Site Snapshot card. Data sent: domain name.

Recommendations (plugin.wedos.global)

  • The signed list of recommendations is downloaded hourly; nothing about your site is sent.
  • When you confirm, ignore or undo a recommendation on a site protected by WEDOS, the plugin reports the domain, the recommendation ID, your decision and the number and average duration of matching requests in the last 24 hours.

Bundled libraries

All code ships inside the plugin package:

  • Chart.js 4.4.0 (MIT): dashboard charts. File assets/vendor/wedos-chart.umd.min.js, an unmodified copy of chart.umd.min.js. Source: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js/releases/tag/v4.4.0
  • jsVectorMap 1.7.0 (MIT, license in assets/vendor/jsvectormap/): the visitor map (paid feature). Source: https://github.com/themustafaomar/jsvectormap
  • WEDOS vulnerability matcher (includes/Vuln/): our own unminified GPL code.

Optionally, the dashboard can load Chart.js and jsVectorMap from wp-cdn.wedos.com instead (switch “Dashboard libraries”). It is off by default; every CDN file carries a Subresource Integrity hash and falls back to the bundled copy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/wgpwpp directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Let the plugin guide you through the service setup process
sections.changelog:
v2.5.1

  • Fix: the dashboard libraries (Chart.js, jsVectorMap) are loaded from the bundled copies by default again; loading them from the WEDOS CDN is the opt-in switch “Dashboard libraries”
  • Plugin description and external services rewritten

v2.5.0

  • Fix: opening the setup page, checking the status or re-syncing the verification token never creates a protection service any more. A service is created only after the consent in the setup, and only when the domain has none: an existing service (also one in another WEDOS account) is only reflected
  • Fix: the DNS records shown are the ones WEDOS Protection asks for (nameservers, CNAME targets, _acme-challenge) instead of generic names; services created in the WEDOS client zone use their own target names. Without ANAME support the A records now point to the protection addresses (previously a CDN address was suggested)
  • Fix: “Active” is shown only when WEDOS Protection reports the service active; while it is still being set up the plugin shows which step it waits for and re-reads the state (with growing intervals, at most once a day once nothing changes)
  • New services are created in record mode, matching the DNS records the plugin shows
  • Re-syncing the verification token no longer queries the WEDOS API
  • Fix: data left in the database by plugin version 1.x is removed on update. Version 2 never used it, but the old option “wgpwpp” could hold a debug log of many megabytes that WordPress loaded on every request (Site Health: autoloaded options)
  • Fix: the daily vulnerability check needed about 170 MB of memory and could fail on hosting with a 128 MB PHP limit. The feed is now downloaded straight to disk and only the entries for installed plugins and themes are read (about 12 MB, 4x faster); the check is skipped when neither the feed nor the installed versions changed

v2.4.0

  • New: detection of the UpdraftCentral key compromise (October 2026): UpdraftCentral keys stored on the website, the hidden backdoor plugin and its secret accounts are shown on the dashboard and in an admin notice, with the steps to take. Read-only: the plugin never changes other plugins, keys or accounts

v2.3.2

  • Fixed: PHP notice “_load_textdomain_just_in_time was called incorrectly” (WordPress 6.7+ with debugging on), caused by translated cron interval labels while the plugin schedules its tasks during load

v2.3.1

  • Fixed: version 2.3.0 on WordPress.org was briefly published without the Recommendations files, which stopped websites that updated during that time
  • New: safety net: if any plugin file is missing (for example after an interrupted update), the plugin pauses itself and shows a notice instead of stopping the website

v2.3.0

  • New: Recommendations — WEDOS publishes signed recommendations, the plugin measures on your site whether they apply and you decide: Confirm or Ignore. Nothing changes without your confirmation and every change can be undone
  • New: first recommendation — requests for missing media files in wp-content/uploads (typically bots) get a fast 404 instead of starting the whole WordPress; applied at web server level (.htaccess) when the server supports it and a check proves it works, otherwise in PHP before the theme loads
  • New: server-level rules are removed again automatically when the plugin is deactivated or WEDOS withdraws the recommendation
  • Security: every request to the WEDOS backend now carries a per-install private key; the verification file publishes only its SHA-256 hash, so nobody else can request this site’s data by naming the domain. The key is created automatically on update and rotates with the verification token
  • Fixed: a failed verification token rotation no longer retries on every dashboard visit; the plugin re-syncs the backend once and retries after 24 hours

v2.2.3

  • Fixed: flushing the whole page cache from the admin bar no longer ends in a fatal error when another request removes a cache folder at the same time; the flush skips the missing folder and clears the rest
  • Fixed: cache maintenance and cache size calculation tolerate files and folders removed concurrently

v2.2.2

  • New: Protection Summary — the dashboard explains in plain words what the protection handled (passed, blocked, verified, logged) and why requests were stopped
  • New: visitor geography with per-country protection actions, connection overview (TLS, HTTP versions) and targeted-paths insight
  • New: security vulnerability scanning of installed plugins, themes and WordPress core against the WEDOS vulnerability feed, with protection-aware guidance
  • New: Site Snapshot daily health card (load time, TTFB, SSL, database, updates, admin accounts) with automatic anomaly notices
  • Improved: onboarding reliably detects an already protected website and opens the dashboard automatically
  • Improved: origin server IP detection never reports the protection edge address as the origin
  • Fixed: page cache no longer stores error responses (database errors, fatal errors); deployed cache runners update themselves
  • Fixed: the verification file is served by WordPress itself when file permissions prevent writing it
  • Security: hardened output escaping and input sanitization across the admin interface

v2.2.1

  • Improved: smart onboarding — the DNS setup step is skipped automatically when the domain already routes to WEDOS Protection (via A records or CNAME/ANAME), including domains protected under another account
  • Improved: DNS records are only required when the protection service reports a known actionable state; active domains are never asked for additional records
  • Improved: WordPress 7.0 compatibility and WordPress.org Plugin Check compliance
  • Fixed: minor onboarding and dashboard polish

v2.2.0

  • New: Visitor Geography section — interactive world map, top countries, top cities, top targeted URI paths with attack-pattern detection, threat distribution and connection quality breakdown (TLS version, encryption ratio, HTTP methods split)
  • New: Subscription plans — Free, Standard and Premium with 30-day free trial that can be started directly from the dashboard
  • New: Security email reports with selectable frequency (weekly or bi-weekly), delivered to the admin email on the configured day
  • New: Daily rotation of the .well-known verification token for hardened ownership proof
  • New: WGP CDN cache purge button — manually flush the Anycast CDN edge cache for sites with a provisioned WGP service
  • Improved: dashboard performance — backend responses are cached locally with smart invalidation on plan changes
  • Improved: refined entitlement system aligned with the subscription plans
